c.tagline: Indonesia's sprawling capital of malls, markets, and endless motorbikes.

taxi.fareNote: Blue Bird is the trusted metered taxi brand; insist on the meter, or use Gojek/Grab for fixed up-front pricing. Avoid unmarked touts at the airport.

emergency.note: 112 is the general nationwide emergency line; 110 reaches police and 113 the fire service.

avoid.reason: Pickpocketing and traffic-jam phone-snatching; caution at demonstrations — use Grab/Gojek.

hood_desc: A leafy, upscale colonial-era district of tree-lined streets, embassies, and museums; central and calm, it suits travelers who want green surroundings within reach of the center.
South Jakarta's expat-favored district packed with bars, cafes, restaurants, and boutiques; the go-to area for nightlife and international dining.
The historic Dutch colonial old town (Kota Tua) around Fatahillah Square, with cobblestone plazas, museums, and the Sunda Kelapa harbor; the city's main sightseeing quarter.
The Sudirman Central Business District, a cluster of gleaming skyscrapers, luxury malls, rooftop bars, and high-end hotels; a modern base for business travelers and upscale nightlife.
The central Thamrin corridor around the Bundaran HI roundabout and Grand Indonesia mall, lined with flagship hotels and transit links; the most convenient walkable base for first-timers.
lodging: The Hermitage, a Tribute Portfolio Hotel

water.note: Stick to bottled or purified water; even locals avoid tap water in Jakarta.

transit.hours: MRT and TransJakarta run roughly 5:00 AM to midnight; the KRL Commuterline runs from around 4:00 AM to midnight. No 24-hour rail service, so ride-hailing fills the late-night gap.
transit.note: Jakarta's rail backbone is the MRT (north-south line), supplemented by the extensive TransJakarta BRT busway network, the KRL Commuterline serving Greater Jakarta (Jabodetabek), and the newer Jakarta LRT and Jabodebek LRT lines.
transit.pay: Most systems use the tap-in JakLingko card or bank e-money cards (as of 2026 the MRT and TransJakarta also accept the JakLingko app and QRIS). Fares are cheap (TransJakarta ~3,500 IDR flat; MRT distance-based).

bus: Intercity buses from Kampung Rambutan, Pulo Gebang, and Kalideres terminals
ferry: Ferries to the Thousand Islands (Kepulauan Seribu) from Ancol Marina and Muara Angke
train: Intercity trains from Gambir and Pasar Senen stations to Bandung, Yogyakarta, and Surabaya

transit.m: Railink airport train to BNI City / Sudirman (~40-55 min)
Damri airport bus to points around the city (~60-90 min)
Blue Bird metered taxi to city center (45-90 min in traffic)

tip.r: Not expected; many restaurants already add a 5-10% service charge. Rounding up or leaving small change for good service is appreciated.

landmarks: National Monument (Monas)
Jakarta's soaring 132-meter obelisk topped with a gold flame is the city's most recognizable symbol and offers panoramic views from its observation deck.
Istiqlal Mosque
Southeast Asia's largest mosque impresses with its vast modernist dome and courtyard, a striking symbol of Indonesia's religious tolerance right across from the cathedral.
Jakarta Cathedral
This neo-Gothic Catholic cathedral's twin spires make a dramatic photo subject, especially framed against its Islamic neighbor Istiqlal Mosque.
Fatahillah Square (Kota Tua/Old Town)
The cobblestoned heart of Dutch colonial Batavia, ringed by museums and colonial architecture, is Jakarta's most atmospheric spot for street photography.
Sunda Kelapa Harbor
This centuries-old wooden-schooner port still bustling with traditional Bugis pinisi ships offers a rare living glimpse of old maritime trade.
Taman Mini Indonesia Indah (TMII)
A sprawling cultural park recreating every Indonesian province in miniature, crowned by the striking Saudjana viewing tower, ideal for a crash course in the archipelago's diversity.
Ancol Dreamland (Taman Impian Jaya Ancol)
Jakarta's premier waterfront recreation area combines a wide beach boardwalk with theme parks, popular for sunset photos over the bay.
National Museum of Indonesia
Known as the 'Elephant Museum', its grand colonial facade and vast archaeological collection make it a must for understanding Indonesian history.
Glodok (Jakarta Chinatown)
One of the world's oldest Chinatowns, its narrow lanes of temples, hawkers, and shophouses offer vibrant, unfiltered street scenes.
Ragunan Zoo
A lush, sprawling 140-hectare zoo famous for its orangutan conservation program, offering a green escape from the megacity's concrete sprawl.

train.note: Indonesia is an archipelago with no international rail. Jakarta is the hub of Java's network: Gambir station handles most executive long-distance trains, Pasar Senen the economy services, and Halim is the terminus of the Whoosh high-speed line to Bandung, which takes about 45 minutes. Overnight trains reach Yogyakarta in 7-8 hours and Surabaya in 9-11. Book on the KAI Access app or booking.kai.id from 45 days out; trains sell out completely around Idul Fitri.

bus.note: No international coaches - Java has no land border. Long-distance buses use Terminal Pulo Gebang in the east and Kampung Rambutan in the south, with operators such as Rosalia Indah, Sinar Jaya and Pahala Kencana running overnight to Yogyakarta, Surabaya and across the Sunda Strait to Sumatra using the Merak ferry. Book through redBus Indonesia (https://www.redbus.id/) or Traveloka; the train is usually more comfortable on Java.

intl.to: Sumatra, Kalimantan, Sulawesi & eastern Indonesia - sails from Tanjung Priok
Thousand Islands / Kepulauan Seribu (Indonesia) - from Marina Ancol and Kali Adem
intl.op: local speedboat operators — tickets at the jetty

ferry.note: There are no international sailings from Jakarta. Pelni's national passenger ships leave from Tanjung Priok, the big port in the north of the city, on long multi-day routes around the archipelago - cheap, slow and an experience in themselves, with tickets sold at the Pelni office or online. The Thousand Islands boats are day-trip transport to the resort islands in the bay, about 90 minutes out.

half.name: Bogor
half.blurb: A cooler hill city about an hour south of Jakarta, built around a large colonial-era botanical garden.

half.name: Puncak
half.blurb: A mountain pass between Bogor and Bandung lined with tea plantations and cooler air than the capital.

full.name: Bandung
full.blurb: A highland city known for Dutch colonial architecture and a cooler climate, about three hours from Jakarta.

full.name: Thousand Islands (Pulau Seribu)
full.blurb: A scattered archipelago in Jakarta Bay reached by boat, with snorkeling and island-hopping among its clearer waters.
